subject: Game Theory
title: Carbon Credit Auctions
description: A 60-second lesson on Carbon Credit Auctions.

hook.text: The EU auctions billions of euros in carbon emission permits every year to fight climate change.

buildup.text: Companies must buy permits to pollute. The auction sets the carbon price, making pollution expensive.

discovery.text: Higher auction prices push firms to cut emissions. The market creates incentives that regulations alone can't.

twist.text: But prices collapsed in 2012 when too many permits flooded the market. Design flaws undermined the goal.

climax.text: The EU reformed by reducing permit supply. Carbon prices jumped from €5 to over €90 per ton.

quiz.question: Why did EU carbon prices collapse in 2012?
options: Too many permits flooded the market
